video.title: The Most Passive Online Side Hustle I've Ever Seen

summary: Chris Koerner argues that simple AI-vibe-coded calculator or tool websites (paycheck, calorie, mortgage, etc.) can earn passive ad and email-lead income because they capture large search volume. He cites big examples (paycheck calculator, calorie calculator, Omni Calculator) and his own pet cremation directory calculators. He then builds an AI token cost calculator in Hostinger Horizons in about 6 minutes, picks the niche with Google Trends, adds email gating and AdSense, and publishes it. Key takeaway: build many cheap niche tool sites, validate with trends and keyword data, and monetise beyond AdSense with email capture and lead sales. The video is sponsored by Hostinger, so the ease claims are promotional.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; serial entrepreneur who says he has started over 80 businesses.

ideas.name: AI-built niche calculator website (AI token cost calculator)
ideas.one_liner: Vibe-code a simple calculator site around a growing search term, monetise with AdSense and email capture, and leave it running.
ideas.business_model: Ads (Google AdSense), email list monetisation (newsletter, affiliate links), possible lead sales.
ideas.customer: People searching Google or AI for a calculator; in the demo, vibe coders and people building with AI tools.
ideas.problem: People want a quick answer (e.g. what AI prompts cost in tokens) and find it hard to work out themselves.
ideas.offer: Free calculator that estimates AI model cost from input and output tokens, with a token counter and tips to cut usage; results unlock after entering an email.

pricing.model: Free to users; revenue from ads and email value

price_points.label: AdSense at about 10,000 page views a month: 30 to 100 USD
Claimed value of an email address

pricing.notes: Hypothetical figures only; the demo site has no revenue yet.

acquisition_channels.details: Pick high or growing search-volume keywords (core and long-tail) using Semrush, Ahrefs or an AI tool, check Google Trends, and add SEO content such as token-reduction tips.

quote.text: Best tool sites solve a very specific problem that have high andor growing search volume.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Site is built by prompting Hostinger Horizons (AI app builder), published on a custom domain, and needs about an hour a week afterwards (claimed). Further calculators can be cloned from the same template.
unit_economics_claims: AdSense at 10,000 monthly page views yields about 30 to 100 USD a month
Email at 1% of 10,000 visitors gives 100 emails, hypothetically about 1,000 USD a month at 10 USD each
Hostinger starter plan allows up to 25 websites
ideas.startup_cost: Hostinger starter plan, 12-month, 10% off with code; the domain is about a cent for year one or a free .cloud domain; the transcript states no total. Builder credits used: 4 of 70 for the month.

acquisition.how: Organic SEO traffic is inbound; keyword research and content can be done by agents. Rankings take time and are uncertain.

onboarding.how: There are no customers to onboard; the visitor just uses the tool.

delivery.how: A static or serverless calculator runs unattended once built; occasional price-data updates can be agent-driven.

billing.how: Ad networks pay out automatically; there are no invoices.

support.how: Low support needs; occasional bug reports or data corrections can be handled by an agent.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK. Email capture needs UK GDPR and PECR consent for marketing, and cookie consent is required for AdSense. UK-relevant calculators (tax, mortgage, student loan) are available. UK ad RPMs may differ.

risks: AdSense revenue is low without large traffic
Rankings are uncertain and AI search or Google AI answers may cut calculator traffic
Easy to copy, so competition is rising
Email gating may reduce usage and hurt SEO
Vibe-coded output can have bugs, e.g. results shown before the email gate

quotes.text: non-coders such as myself can vibe code simple sites like these, forget about it entirely, and maybe hopefully possibly make hundreds or thousands or tens of thousands of dollars a month almost perfectly passively

tactics.name: Find supply and demand imbalances in keywords
steps: Use Semrush, Ahrefs or an AI tool to list core and long-tail keywords
Look for terms with higher volume but fewer competitors

lessons.lesson: Cheap, fast experiments suit small web tools: the downside is a few dollars and a few hours, so ship more and overthink less.

quote.text: your downside is a few bucks and a couple hours of tinkering around.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Validate demand with search-trend data before building, not by guessing.

quote.text: I don't want to guess. I want data to show me.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Single-purpose utility sites can earn from traffic with no customers, sales or support, which makes them well suited to agent-run operations.
Ride rising trends (AI, GLP-1s, solar, protein, side hustles) where supply of tools lags demand.
Capture emails as well as ad revenue, since a subscriber list can be worth far more than AdSense per visitor (a hypothetical claim).
Pair calculators with a lead-gen directory: a calculator can pull in traffic and capture leads that are sold to providers.
Choose a niche you know and love so the project is more sustainable.

quote.text: it's important that you choose a niche that you love and that you know.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use the sunk-cost effect carefully: the more effort a user invests before the email ask, the more likely they are to give it.

evidence_quality.rationale: Sponsored tutorial. Traffic and valuation figures for third-party sites are unsourced hearsay, revenue projections are hypothetical, and the demo site has no revenue yet. The build process is shown first-hand, but the 'passive' income claim is unproven.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsored by Hostinger (Horizons); the host promotes the code kerner office for 10% off and likely earns affiliate income.
